title: HiSpTRSV: Exploring Tile-Level Parallelism for SpTRSV Acceleration on FPGAs
problem: Sparse Triangular Solve (SpTRSV) in sparse BLAS is a critical level-2 kernel with inherent data dependencies; existing FPGA accelerators focus only on intra-tile parallelism, missing inter-tile parallelism opportunities due to challenges in dependency graph construction, communication overhead, and workload balancing.
motivation: Efficient SpTRSV acceleration on heterogeneous accelerators is needed for sparse linear algebra workloads in scientific computing and machine learning; exploiting multiple levels of parallelism can significantly improve performance.
method: HiSpTRSV designs tile-based highly parallel algorithm leveraging inter-tile parallelism through dependency graph parsing, tile-based parallelization, filtering mechanisms, and bidirectional matching with modular indexing to handle communication overhead and workload distribution.
key_novelty: First FPGA accelerator for SpTRSV exploiting inter-tile parallelism beyond intra-tile computation, addressing communication and workload balance challenges.
contributions: Fine-grained dependency graph parsing enabling inter-tile parallelism extraction
Tile-based parallel algorithm with filtering mechanisms for dependency optimization
Bidirectional matching with modular indexing for efficient communication
34.3% performance improvement vs. SOTA SpTRSV accelerator, 3.58x vs. GPU, 9.59x energy efficiency vs. GPU

metrics.speedup: 3.58x vs. GPU, 34.3% vs. SOTA SpTRSV accelerator

primary_theme: FPGA-based sparse triangular solver with inter-tile parallelism
